rationale: Both candidates correctly reconstruct the only substantive ground-truth concern (the trust_remote_code/kernels-0.13.x issue) and recognize it was already fixed by a later commit, and both independently surface the same solid secondary finding (no test exercises the new cache/fallback path) plus the stale PR description and the unexplained NPU CI failure. X adds a genuinely novel, well-reasoned point (broad except-clause makes a transient network failure 'sticky' via the cache) and stays cleanly organized and readable. Y's findings are extremely well-evidenced with exact quotes and even includes actionable suggestion diffs, but the output is cluttered with duplicated 'validated' bullets and leaks irrelevant internal tool/skill-store metadata, hurting actionability.
